walkthroughs.body_html:
The Changing Economic World — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Changing Economic World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Changing Economic World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What happens in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?
options: Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Death rates fall rapidly (due to better food, sanitation and medicine) while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Birth rates rise rapidly because people want larger families.

mcqs.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
options: Through hydraulic action (water compressing air in cracks), abrasion (waves throwing rocks against cliffs), attrition (rocks smashing against each other), and solution.
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Waves erode cliffs by pushing water against the rock until it breaks.
